record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: Can the stable entropy-computation algorithm known for orthogonal polynomials on a bounded interval be extended, or replaced by another stable method, for orthogonality on an unbounded interval?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 5.3. Is it possible to extend this method (or to find an alternative one) for the case of the unbounded interval of orthogonality?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu$ be a positive Borel measure on an unbounded interval $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ (for instance $I=[0,\infty)$ or $I=\mathbb{R}$) for which all moments are finite, and let $\{p_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be the sequence of polynomials orthonormal with respect to $\mu$, satisfying the three-term recurrence
$$x p_n(x) = a_{n+1} p_{n+1}(x) + b_n p_n(x) + a_n p_{n-1}(x), \qquad n \ge 0,$$
with recurrence coefficients $\{a_n, b_n\}$. Define the (differential) entropy of $p_n$ with respect to the orthogonality measure by
$$E_n(\mu) := -\int_I p_n(x)^2 \log igl(p_n(x)^2 igr)\, d\mu(x).$$

For measures supported on a bounded interval there exists a numerically stable algorithm that computes $E_n(\mu)$ taking as input only the recurrence coefficients $\{a_k, b_k\}_{k=0}^{n}$.

Problem: Devise a numerically stable algorithm that, given only the recurrence coefficients $\{a_k, b_k\}$ associated with a measure $\mu$ on an unbounded interval $I$, computes the entropy $E_n(\mu)$ for each $n$. Equivalently, either extend the bounded-interval method to the unbounded case, or design an alternative stable method valid for unbounded intervals of orthogonality.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results show that a stable entropy-computation algorithm for polynomials orthogonal on a bounded interval is well established (Buyarov et al., SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 2004), and there is ongoing work on stable computation of recurrence coefficients on unbounded supports. However, no source clearly establishes a fully analogous stable entropy-computation method for orthogonality on unbounded intervals, and the status of the question appears unresolved from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Computation of the Entropy of Polynomials Orthogonal on an Interval
status_evidence.snippet: An effective method for computing the entropy for polynomials orthogonal on a segment of the real axis, taking as input data only the coefficients of the recurrence relation.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the stable bounded-interval entropy algorithm referenced as the starting point of the question.

status_evidence.title: On the computation of recurrence coefficients for univariate orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms can compute recurrence coefficients of continuous orthogonal polynomials with respect to measures on bounded or unbounded supports.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates progress on stable numerical handling of unbounded supports, but does not specifically resolve stable entropy computation.

status_evidence.title: Quantum information entropies and orthogonal polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of entropy results for orthogonal polynomials including classical families on unbounded intervals.
status_evidence.claim: Discusses entropies for unbounded-interval orthogonal polynomials but does not provide a general stable algorithm of the requested type.
